intro: The first skateboards were planks of wood with metal roller-skate wheels nailed on. Surfers in California rode them on sidewalks when the ocean was flat. By the mid-1960s, companies sold boards in stores, and a national contest was on TV. Then the craze faded, because the wheels slipped, jammed and threw riders off.

In the 1970s, a new wheel made of urethane changed everything. It gripped the ground and rolled over cracks. A kicktail let riders lift the nose. Smooth bearings spun longer. A team from Santa Monica brought a low surf style, and empty pools in a drought gave skaters curved walls to ride.

In this unit you will meet the people, places and inventions of skateboarding's first two booms. You will learn why a hard wheel stops at a pebble and why a soft one rolls on. You will practice a tail press safely. You will see how energy changes on a curved wall.
bigQuestion: How did better wheels and new places to ride turn a fading fad into a lasting sport?

timeline.t: Surfers in California ride homemade boards on sidewalks
Larry Stevenson starts the Makaha skateboard company
First National Skateboard Championships in Anaheim, shown on TV
Patti McGee wins the women's title and appears on the cover of Life
The first boom fades as riders get hurt on poor wheels
Larry Stevenson's kicktail patent is granted
Frank Nasworthy's Cadillac Wheels bring urethane to skateboards
The Zephyr team rides at the Del Mar Nationals
Drought leaves California pools empty; skaters ride their walls
Carlsbad Skatepark and Skateboard City open

the metal parts under the deck that hold the wheels and let the board turn
hard wheels made of a pressed mix of materials, used on many 1960s boards
the way a moving thing keeps moving until a push or pull changes it
a time when something becomes popular and grows very fast
a tough plastic that bends a little and springs back; used for modern wheels
a force between two surfaces that pushes against sliding
a tool and number scale that measure how hard a material is, like a wheel
the back end of a board that bends upward so a rider can press it
a ring of small balls inside a wheel that lets it spin smoothly
the curved part where a flat floor bends up into a wall
a place built for skateboarding, with ramps, bowls and curved walls

test.q: Who first rode skateboards on California sidewalks in the late 1950s?
test.why: Surfers and kids in California rode boards on sidewalks when the waves were flat.

test.q: What were the wheels on the first homemade boards?
test.why: Kids took metal wheels from roller skates for the first boards.

test.q: In what year did Larry Stevenson start Makaha?
Where were the first National Skateboard Championships held in 1965?
test.why: The 1965 championships took place in Anaheim, California.

test.q: Which rider was the 1965 women's champion and on the cover of Life?
test.why: Patti McGee won the 1965 women's title and was on Life's cover.

test.q: Why did clay wheels throw riders off in turns?
choices: They did not grip and slid sideways.
test.why: Clay wheels had poor grip, so they slid out on turns.

test.q: A board hits a pebble and stops, but the rider keeps going. What idea explains this?
test.why: Inertia: a moving body keeps moving until a push or pull stops it.

test.q: Why did the first boom fade around 1965 to 1966?
choices: Many riders got hurt on poor wheels.
test.why: Clay and steel wheels slipped and jammed, and many riders got hurt.

test.q: What new wheel material did Frank Nasworthy bring to skateboarding?
test.why: Frank Nasworthy brought urethane wheels to skateboarding in the early 1970s.
On the durometer A scale, the smallest number is the softest wheel.

test.q: What did Larry Stevenson's 1971 patent cover?
test.why: Stevenson's patent, granted in 1971, was for the kicktail.

test.q: In a tail press, where does the front foot go?
test.why: The front foot rests across the board just behind the front bolts; the back foot is on the tail.

test.q: Which riders were on the Zephyr team?
choices: Peggy Oki, Tony Alva, Jay Adams and Stacy Peralta
test.why: Peggy Oki, Tony Alva, Jay Adams and Stacy Peralta rode for Zephyr.

test.q: Why did many California pools sit empty in 1976 and 1977?
choices: There was a drought, and water was scarce.
test.why: A drought made water scarce, so many pools were drained or left empty.

test.q: As a skater rolls up a curved wall and slows down, what is the motion energy changing into?
test.why: Going up the wall, motion energy changes into stored energy.

write.prompt: Explain how skateboarding changed from 1965 to 1976. Name at least two people, two dates and two inventions, and tell why the new wheel made such a big difference.
tips: Start with the problems of clay and steel wheels.
Use dates like 1965, 1971, 1975 and 1976 in order.
Name people such as Patti McGee, Larry Stevenson, Frank Nasworthy or Peggy Oki.
Use the words friction and grip to explain the urethane wheel.
